subject: SLO qualification playbook & reproducibility checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: SLO qualification playbook & reproducibility checklist

Hi Sam — great call this morning, thanks for walking through the FastRetail streaming checkout flow. Quick recap and agreed handoff items so we have a single source of truth: 

- Latency targets: 95th %ile < 180 ms for single-turn suggestions (seq len ~128); 95th %ile streaming token latency target < 70 ms token-to-token under realistic concurrency.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline test should validate sustained 600 reqs/min with p95 latency SLO; spike test to 1.5x for 2m.
- Streaming: client uses chunked tokens; we will validate prefix caching behavior and cold-start token latencies (first token).
- Repro & harness: we'll exchange the prompt seed, the measurement spec, and a minimal harness (run config + sanity checks).

Deliverables (owners & ETA):
- prompt_seed_v1.jsonl — Jordan (handoff by EOD 11/05) [attached]
- harness-instructions.md — Ben (draft by 11/06)
- measurement-spec.md (definitions for p50/p90/p95, token accounting, warm/cold run rules) — Ben
- run-config.yaml example for the harness (env, seq_len distribution, concurrency profile) — Marissa

Can you confirm the acceptance criteria below so we can schedule the eng handoff next week?
1) Repro run reproduces p95 within +/- 10% of your production baseline for the same workload.
2) No ordering differences in token outputs between local harness and Redwood runtime for the canonical prompt set (we'll provide a diff tool).
3) Runs include both cold-start and warmed cache profiles (minimum 3 runs each).

I'm attaching the initial prompt seed and a short harness note. If that looks good we'll lock a 60-minute handoff slot for Tue 11/09 with eng & SRE.

Thanks,
--
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLO qualification playbook & reproducibility checklist

Thanks Jordan — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications before you share artifacts: 

- For the streaming token latency target (p95 < 70 ms), is that measured per-token after the first token or including first-token overhead? Our client instrumentation measures both and we need to align.
- On the throughput side, our nominal traffic shape is spiky (mornings: short burst at ~2x baseline). Can the run-config represent a burst profile and a steady-state profile?
- About the reproducibility check: will you require exact token-for-token equality or a soft-match (semantic similarity threshold)? We've seen minor non-determinism across runs when using different batching.

Also, can you share how Redwood treats KV cache warmup in the run rules? We want to confirm the 'warmed cache' profile you mentioned.

Sam
Senior Engineering Manager, FastRetail
sam.h@fastretail.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Hendricks <sam.h@fastretail.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2026 15:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO qualification playbook & reproducibility checklist

Sam — good questions. Quick answers and an attached sketch of the measurement rules (measurement-spec.md) + a run-config example. Highlights: 

- Streaming token latency: we measure both first-token and per-token steady-state. The p95 < 70 ms target applies to per-token steady-state (token-to-token) after the first token. We'll report first-token p95 separately and suggest a separate threshold (we had < 260 ms in similar workloads).
- Repro check: canonical run uses exact-token equality for the canonical prompt set (this is the strict gate). For broader prompt families we provide a soft-match pipeline (BLEU / normalized edit distance + model-similarity score). The harness includes flags to run strict vs fuzzy checks.
- KV cache warmup: warmed profile = priming the model with 50 representative requests matching the user's prefix distribution, followed by a 30s steady window. Cold runs start from an empty cache. The run-config has fields to control priming size and steady window.

Attachments: measurement-spec.md (rules & metrics), run-config.yaml (example).

Next steps: Ben will produce a reproducibility checklist and a small diff tool for token comparisons by 11/06. If that timeline changes I'll update the thread.

--
